names.name: Perumāḷ / Emperumāṉ (the Great One / our Lord)
Tiruvaraṅkaṉ, Tiruvēṅkaṭamuṭaiyāṉ and the other names of the Lord at each sung site

descriptions: He who has the highest good, beyond which there is nothing higher; lord of the unwearying immortals; whose radiant feet end sorrow (TVM 1.1.1).
When there was no god, no world and no life, he created the four-faced Brahmā with the gods, worlds and lives (TVM 4.10.1); Nārāyaṇa made Brahmā and Brahmā made Śaṅkara (Nāṉmukaṉ Tiruvantāti 1).
He pervades all things hidden within them as life within a body (TVM 1.1.7).
Easy of access to those who love him, hard to reach for others (TVM 1.3.1); he takes whatever form and name his devotees delight in (Mutal Tiruvantāti 44).
He dwells with Śrī on his chest, who says she cannot part from him even for a moment (TVM 6.10.10).
He is present in the temple image at Śrīraṅgam, Tiruvēṅkaṭam and the other sung sites, awakened at dawn, praised with benedictions for his own safety (Tiruppallāṇṭu; Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci).
negations: Not one god among many: the Āḻvārs repeatedly deny that the other gods are refuges (Nāṉmukaṉ Tiruvantāti; Madhurakavi's 'I know no other god' is said of his teacher).
relation_to_self: The self belongs to the Lord as servant to master: 'I thought I was my own and what I had was mine; I am yours and what I have is yours' (TVM 2.9.9); its fulfilment is faultless service at all times (TVM 3.3.1).
relation_to_world: The world and lives are his creation and his body; he is hidden in them as life in a body (TVM 1.1.7) and swallowed and restored them (the 'world-swallower' image); the world is real and is the field of his play and avatāras.
caveat: The Āḻvārs and the Śrīvaiṣṇava commentators would reject any one-truth reading that makes Nārāyaṇa one name among equals for an impersonal absolute or that treats Śiva, Brahmā or other gods as independent refuges; the Lord is one, but he is Nārāyaṇa with Śrī, personal and qualified.

names.name: Hari, Kṛṣṇa (as the object of the gopīs' love, NBS 21)

descriptions: The Lord who, when sung of, quickly manifests himself and makes his devotees experience him (NBS 80).
The Lord dislikes pride and loves humility (NBS 27).
Love for him (prema) is indescribable, like a mute's tasting; free of the guṇas and of desire, increasing every moment, unbroken, subtlest, of the nature of experience (NBS 51–54).
Three views of the object of devotion: the Lord's majesty as other (Kāśyapa), the one self (Bādarāyaṇa), both (Śāṇḍilya) (ŚBS, as recalled).
relation_to_self: Devotees are 'His own' (tadīya, NBS 73); there is no difference between the Lord and his people (NBS 41). ŚBS: Śāṇḍilya holds devotion bears on both the Lord as other and the self as one (low confidence on the exact sūtras).
relation_to_world: Worldly and Vedic activity is to be laid down in him (nirodha, NBS 8); until love is attained worldly activity is not abandoned but its fruit is given up (NBS 62).
caveat: The bhakti-śāstra would reject a one-truth reading that makes devotion a preparatory stage to be surpassed by impersonal knowledge: for the Nārada Sūtra love is the fruit itself (NBS 26, 30).
